INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport,
Tourism and Culture, having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Forty-third Report on “Action Taken by the Government on the
Recommendation/Observations of the Committee contained in its One Hundred and Thirty-fourth
Report on Demands for Grants 2008-09 of the Department of Shipping”.
2. The One Hundred and Thirty-fourth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented to the Parliament on the
17th April, 2008.
3. The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained on its
One Hundred and Thirty-fourth Report were received from the Department of Shipping on the 23rd
October, 2008.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the
18th December, 2008.
SITARAM YECHURY
N
EW D ELHI; Chairman,
December 18, 2008 Department-related Parliamentary Standing
Agrahayana 27, 1930  (Saka) Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture.

1
REPORT
This Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
observations/recommendations as contained in its One Hundred Thirty-fourth Report on Demands
for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Shipping, which was presented to the Parliament on
17th April, 2008.
2. Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on 23rd October, 2008 in
respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report. These have been
categorized as follows:—
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 10, 11, 28, 48, 55, 63, 64, 70, 81, 82 and 97 Total: 11
(ii) Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view
of the Government replies:
Para Nos. 39 and 101 Total: 2
(iii) R ecommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been
accepted by the Committee:
Para Nos. 100 Total :1
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still
awaited:
Para Nos. 16, 20, 23, 24, 31, 35, 40, 51, 58, 69, 75, 93 and 94 Total :13
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which
have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the
earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each
item of the action taken/proposed to be taken by the Department of Shipping. The
recommendations of the Committee contained in the One Hundred Thirty-fourth Report, action
taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each
item of action taken have been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2008-09
(Recommendation at Para 10 and 11))
5. The Committee observes that the Department has projected a requirement of Rs.68971.48
crore for the entire Eleventh Plan. Against this requirement, the Planning Commission approved an
allocation of Rs. 67173.40 crore to the Department for carrying out major activities i.e.
development of Major Ports, Inland Water Transport, procurement of Dredgers and connected
activities for the Dredging Corporation of India, constructions of landing facility in Andaman and
Nicobar Islands, post Tsunami rehabilitation works, Ship Buidling, Rail connectivity for the ports
and Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project etc.
6. The Committee strongly deplores the tendency of Planning Commission and the Ministry of
Finance for imposing cuts on the amount demanded by the Department as per their pressing needs.

2
The Committee feels that if the Department of Shipping has to attain the national growth of 9%
in the Eleventh Plan period, it will require huge and well planned funding. Thus, the Government
spending for the Department of Shipping will have to be significantly stepped up from the present
level to meet the growth targets. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the
Department should be provided with Rs.68971.48 crore by the Planning Commission and the
Ministry of Finance for the Eleventh Plan period as their original proposal and ensure that no
projects/scheme proposed by the Department would languish for want of funds. The Committee
also recommends the Department to take appropriate caution and remedial action to absorb in time
the allocation made to them.
Reply of the Government
7. The recommendations of the Committee have been brought to the notice of Planning
Commission as well as Ministry of Finance for compliance.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
8. The Committee notes that as per the recommendations of the Committee, the
Department of Shipping has requested the Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance for
providing Rs.68971.48 crore as per original proposal for the entire Eleventh  Plan. The
Committee feels that if the Department has to achieve the growth targets then the Planning
Commission and Ministry of Finance should consider to allocate the projected outlay.
PORT SECTOR
(Recommendation at Paras 16 and 20)
9. The Committee is perturbed to note that the Department of Shipping has projected higher
plan outlays of Rs.4271.27 crore during the year 2007-08 which was drastically reduced to
Rs.3075.34 crore at RE stage and ultimately, the Department failed to utilize the reduced amount
too. The Department utilized Rs.2517.00 crore during 2007-08 against the budget estimates of
Rs.4271.27 crore and surrendered an amount of Rs.1754.27 crore as compared to the BE for the
year. The Committee observes that the saving affects almost all the major activities of Department
of Shipping be it Inland Water Transport, Shipping, Ports, Lighthouses and Lightships, Shipbuilding
etc. and the actual expenditure incurred has always been abysmally low compared to the estimated
amount. The Committee is not satisfied with the reasons furnished by the Department for non-
utilization of the allocations for their being either vague or of routine in nature. The Committee does
not approve the practice being followed by the Department which has been asking for higher
allocations year after year, but the implementation of projects and schemes were poor as ground
realities were not taken into account while formulating and implementing the projects. The
Committee is pained to note that although they have repeatedly recommended for formulation of
realistic plans and schemes but no action have been taken by the Government on those
recommendations. The Committee expects that intensified monitoring mechanism which is being put
in place by the Department, would ensure that budgeted amounts earmarked at the BE stage are
fully utilized during 2008-09. At the same time, The Committee recommends that a meaningful and
relevant programmes and policies be formulated for regular infusion of funds in various projects
and schemes in all quarters of the financial year for total utilization of plan outlays and if required,
the Government should review all the on-going schemes periodically for re-allocation of the
budgeted amount. The Committee would like to be apprised of the action taken by the Government
in this regard.
10. The Committee is distressed to note that there has been under-utilization of plan allocation
in the port sector and finds that in BE 2007-08, an outlay of Rs.2109.76 crore consisting of GBS

3
of Rs.498.49 crore and IEBR of Rs.1611.27 crore was provided to the port sector as against this
allocation, the anticipated expenditure is Rs.1694.71 crore comprising of Rs.359.62 crore GBS and
Rs.1335.09 crore IEBR. In the Annual Plan 2008-09, again higher budgetary allocations to
Rs.3650.97 crore has been made in anticipation of modernization of port sector though the actual
expenditure has always remain low as compared to budget estimates. The Committee feels that
since ports have a crucial role to play in facilitating the India’s total EXIM trade, the Department
should devise the concrete and concerted efforts for achieving the desired targets. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that projections of required fund should be made more realistic so that
resources are not unnecessarily kept unutilized and are allocated more judiciously and projects are
monitored scrupulously to achieve the envisaged targets. The Committee would also like to be
apprised of the achievement of the physical and financial targets in the port sector during the
current financial year.
Reply of the Government
11. The above recommendations of the Committee have been forwarded to all the Major Ports
and other concerned Organizations for compliance.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
12. The Committee notes the reply and desires to have the expenditure pattern of the
Department of Shipping for the year 2007-08 and 2008-09 up to December, 2008 to ascertain
the progress of fiscal management, utilization of budgetary allocation and the details of the
physical and financial target set for achieving the progress. The Committee recommends
that for better physical and financial monitoring of the projects, the Department should
strengthen its own monitoring mechanism in a well coordinated manner at apex level to
achieve optimum utilization of funds.
(Recommendation at Para 23 and 24)
13. The Committee notes that the Department has delegated the financial powers to the port
trusts under the instructions issued by the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance for
timely execution, formulation, appraisal and approval of the projects to be funded through the
public investment and also for public private partnership projects. The respective jurisdiction with
respect to Standing Finance Committee (SFC), Departmental Expenditure Finance Committee
(Departmental EFC), Main Expenditure Finance Committee (Main EFC), Committee of Secretaries
(CoS), Public Investment Board (PIB) or Public Private Partnership Appraisal Committee (PPPAC)
is determined on the basis of the total cost of the project/schemes for the entire plan period. The
Committee notes with dismay that the spreparation and clearance of SFC/EFC/CCEA/PPPAC
proposals require undue long time and in some cases it takes precious long time of about 2-3
years. The Committee see no justification in such a situation wherein many schemes/plans/projects
of the Department has an outlay for a period of 5 years mentioned on paper only but actually
cannot be utilized till the approval of the SFC/EFC/CCEA/PPPAC remains pending. The Committee
urges the Department as well as the concerned Appraisal Agencies to seriously introspect over
the delays which are so detrimental for the progressive functioning of the Shipping and Port
Sectors.
14. The Committee also desires that steps should be taken well in time by the Department/
Planning Commission/Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) to avoid any such
recurrences for the future and a limited stipulated time frame should be fixed for clearance from
the Planning Commission and SFC/EFC/CCEA/PPPAC approval.

4
Reply to the Government
15. The recommendations of the Committee have been brought to the notice of Planning
Commission as well as Ministry of Finance for compliance.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
16. The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping has taken up the matter with
the Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance for removal of procedural hurdles in the
preparation and clearance of project proposals. The Committee does not see any difficulty in
the Government establishing a single high powered agency for quick clearance of projects
proposals for the Shipping and Port Sectors with a view to address the procedural hurdles and
administrative delays. The Committee therefore, recommends the Department to pursue the
matter with the Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance for setting up of the single
high powered Committee for the progressive functioning of the Shipping and Port Sector.
CAPACITY UPGRADATION IN MAJOR PORTS
(Recommendation at Para 28)
17. The Committee takes note of the efforts being made by the Department of Shipping in
implementing schemes for augmenting the cargo handling capacity and productivity of all major
ports under National Maritime Development Programme (NMDP) to meet India’s EXIM trade
requirements. The Committee also notes that during 2007-08, the aggregate capacity of major ports
was 504.75 mt pa which was a little over the total traffic of 469.37 mt. up to February, 2008.
The Committee feels that the projected increase in the traffic also requires increase in capacity in
ports. During Eleventh Plan period, the ports require a projected capacity addition of 1016.55 mt pa
to meet the overall projected traffic of 1008.95 mt. of which the share of major ports will be
708.09 mt. The Committee also observes that the bulk of capacity augmentation projects at major
ports will be undertaken through Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) and captive users. The
Committee recommends the Department of Shipping to devise plans for holistic and integrated
development of major ports and make efforts to encourage the private sector investments including
FDI for creation and maintenance of port infrastructure including cargo handling capacity at major
ports. The Committee also recommends the Department to provide enabling policies, regulatory
framework and institutional monitoring mechanism support to raise port efficiency, productivity,
equipment and performance level in order to face global challenges of merchandize trade.
Reply of the Government
18. Noted for compliance.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
19. The Committee notes that as per its recommendation the Department has taken
steps for augmenting capacity building schemes at major Ports for the Eleventh Plan. The
Committee recommends the Department to remove the bottlenecks and provide facilitative
and legislative support to encourage the private sector investments for major capacity
upgradation infrastructure projects at all major Ports.
CONTAINERIZATION IN MAJOR PORTS
(Recommendation at Para 31)
20. The Committee notes that containerization of traffic is growing steadily and significantly

5
with dedicated capacity for handling containerized cargo in major ports. The Committee, however,
is constrained to note that the major ports did not significantly contribute to merchandise global
trade making thereby India’s export costlier and imports less competitive. The Committee observes
that a high powered committee has been constituted by the Government to report on the matter
of creation of infrastructure facilities for handling containers at major ports, identification of
problems of congestion and explore areas of improvement in logistics chain and to suggest
measures to increase India’s share in world maritime trade as in India only two regional hub ports
are operational at Jawaharlal Nehru and Chennai Ports for maximizing direct to destination cargo.
The report of high powered committee is awaited. The Committee recommends the Department of
Shipping to ensure that there is no laxity in its efforts pending report of the high powered
Committee for development of more hub ports in the country for transshipment of containerized
cargo for growth of overseas maritime merchandise trade.
Reply of the Government
21. Noted. The Department of Shipping is planning to construct a number of container
terminals on BOT basis through Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode at various Major Ports.
Some of the container terminals which are expected to be awarded in the next two years are as
shown below:
(i) Container Terminal at Ennore — Estimated cost Rs.1300 crore.
(ii) Mega Container Terminal at Chennai — Estimated cost Rs.3105 crore.
(iii) Container Terminal at Tuticorin — Estimated cost Rs.150 crore
(iv) Container T erminal at Kolkata — Estimated cost Rs.1233 crore
(v) Development of Container Terminal north of NSICT, Jawaharlal Nehru Port–Estimated
cost Rs. 600 crore
(vi) Fourth C ontainer Terminal at Jawaharlal Nehru Port–Estimated cost Rs.4100 crore.
22. In addition License Agreements have been signed for (i) International Container
Transshipment Terminal at Cochin Port which is expected to be operational by November, 2009
(ii) Development of 2nd Container Terminal at Chennai Port which is expected to be operational
by 2009-10 and (iii) Construction of two offshore container terminals at Mumbai Port which is
expected to be operational by 2010-11.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
23. The Committee notes the reply.
PORT CONNECTIVITY
(Recommendation at Para 35)
24. The Committee is perturbed to note that port efficiency is still continuing to be impeded
mainly because of slow evacuation of cargo from ports. It also notes with dismay that various rail-
road connectivity projects in the ports of Haldia, Paradip,Chennai, Ennore, Tuticorin, Cochin, New
Mangalore, Mormugaon, Jawaharlal Nehru Ports are either lagging behind schedule or not
sanctioned for implementation. The Committee feels that the slow progress of projects not only
undermines the competitiveness of Indian Ports but also vitiates the environment of investment in
the country. The Committee recommends the Department to augment the rail-road connectivity of

6
major ports with the hinterland for smooth flow of present as well as future traffic. The Committee
also recommends the Department to fix some realistic and achievable targets and put in place
institutional monitoring and review mechanism so that projects could be completed in a time bound
manner and in case of delay, the responsibility must be fixed.

Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
80. The Committee notes with dismay that the infrastructure required to make the total
transport cost competitive from origin to destination using IWT mode is yet to be developed
namely fairway for safe and unhindered navigation, terminals with mechanical loading/
unloading and aids for 24 hrs navigation. It however, notes that the utilization of the
National Waterways for transportation of cargo is expected to increase significantly after
completion of the implementation of Action Plan and demonstration vessel runs. The targets
for cargo transportation on three existing National Waterways have already been envisaged
in the action plan. The Committee further notes that a study has been awarded to National
Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) for comparison of the cost and benefits of
inland waterways transportation with the alternative modes. The Committee recommends
the Department to provide adequate investment, policy framework and focused approached
for development of these existing national waterways for making them commercially viable.
The Committee would like to be apprised about the details of study report.
(Recommendation at Para 97)
81. The Committee notes with anguish that no security personnel are being provided for safe
transportation of men and material in Sunderbans /Protocol routes in West Bengal. The Committee
is of the opinion that security is a prime concern and should be looked into seriously by making
commensurate security arrangement in Sunderbans/Protocol routes. The Committee recommends
the Department of Shipping to take up the matter of beefing up of security arrangement in the
Sunderbans /Protocol routes with the Union Home Ministry so that inadequacy of police deployment
could be addressed in a big way.
Reply of the Government
82. The DoS or IWAI has not experienced any problem in respect of security arrangements in
Sunderbans/Protocol routes.
83. Under the IWT Trade and Transit Protocol between the Government of Bangladesh and the
Government of India, IWAI is the nodal agency in India for issuing necessary permission for inland
barges of Bangladesh and India for their movement across the country and undertaking loading/
unloading operation at designated Ports of Call. Checking of un-authorized/illegal transportation of
men and materials (cargo) falls under the purview of Customs Department (for material) and
Immigration Department (for men) and IWAI do not play any role in the same. The above two
authorities, at their respective check points, check and verify if the cargo carried by them and the
men present on board the ship are as per the declared manifesto (certified by BIWTA, the nodal
agency on Trade and Transit Protocol on behalf of Bangladesh Government). At all other border
points the Border Security Force keeps vigil on illegal immigrants/illegal movement of goods.
Bangladeshi vessels never demanded from IWAI, security arrangement in their vessels nor have the
State Government of West Bengal/Assam ever requested for security arrangement in Bangladeshi
vessels.

20
84. Nevertheless, the matter had been taken up with the Ministry of Home Affairs who have
replied that the area around the International Border (IB) is dominated properly by BSF with the
help of floating BOP and other water crafts stationed at Bharikhal. No case either of dacoity or
theft, within the jurisdiction of BSF, in this area has been reported. The depth areas, however, are
not under the BSF area of operations. For these area security needs to be ensured by State police,
Coast Guard and Custom officials. Letter have been sent to these agencies.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
85. The Committee notes the reply that the Department has not experienced any
problem in respect of security arrangement in the Sunderbans/protocol routes. However, the
Committee recommends the Department to take up the matter for strengthening the
security arrangements at depth areas which are not under the BSF operations, with the
State police, coast guard and custom officials in the Sunderban/protocol routes, for safe
transportation of men and material.
CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION
(Recommendation at Para 100)
86. The Committee is pained to note that the Government has decided neither to consider
revival of CIWTC nor to amalgamate this Corporation with various Organizations, such as Inland
Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of India
(SCI) that too, without getting conducted any scientific study by an expert agency. The Committee
is of the view that the matter of revival and amalgamation of CIWTC should be got examined by
some high powered expert committee. The Committee once again reiterates its earlier
recommendation contained in 117th Report on Demands for Grants 2007-08 of Department of
Shipping, which is reproduced below:
“The Committee is constrained to note that in spite of its recommendation in the past, the
Government has not come out a complete blueprint for making full use of the existing
assets of River Service Division (RSD). The Committee is of the opinion that CIWTC with
its infrastructure and expertise can play an integral part for development and promotion of
inland water transport through NW-1 and NW-2. The Committee recommends that
possibility may also be explored to physically amalgamate the remaining CIWTC with Inland
Waterway Authority of India (IWAI) or Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation
of India (SCI), so that the infrastructure and expertise of CIWTC can be utilized for
development of waterways transport.”
Reply of the Government
87. It is submitted that the Cabinet has decided in favour of disinvestment of CIWTC minus
RBD. Action has already been initiated in compliance of the said decision. The Corporation has been
making losses continuously since operation in the longer stretches of national waterways as of now
are not commercially viable compelling the Government to go for its disinvestment. The
disinvestment of CIWTC is not likely to affect the role/activities of CIWTC. It will only result in
charge of share holding pattern and in the nomenclature of the Corporation. The Inland Water
Transport activities too are not likely to be affected by the disinvestment of the Corporation.
Further, since Cabinet has already decided in favour of disinvestment of CIWTC (minus RBD), no
feasibility study for merger of CIWTC with other organizations was conducted. The issue of
physical amalgamation of CIWTC (minus RBD) with various organizations such as IWAI, KoPT or
SCI was raised in various communications received from Hon’ble Members of Parliament and other
dignitaries and was examined in the Ministry and not found feasible.

21
88. The corporation has about 100 IWT vessels out of which 40 are operational. While some
of the non-operational vessels are awaiting repair some are beyond economic repair. CIWTC
operated 47 voyages in NW-1 between 2004 and 2006 at the behest of IWAI. The route is,
however, non-economical.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
89. T he Committee is perturbed to note that despite being recommended by the
Committee a number of times the Government has not taken setps to improve the financial
health of the CIWTC. The Committee does not agree with the Government that with the
disinvestment of CIWTC, the role and activities of CIWTC will not be affected. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends the Department to conduct a feasibility study
for merger of CIWTC with other organizations such as IWAI, KoPT or SCI for the holistic
development of inland water transport.
DEVELOPMENT OF WATER TRANSPORT IN ANDAMAN AND NICOBAR AND
LAKSHADWEEP ISLANDS
(Recommendation at Para 101)
90. The Shipping Corporation of India with its two owned passenger-cum-cargo vessels and 27
managed vessels operates domestic passenger-cum-transportation services between mainland and
Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep group of islands on behalf of the Government of
India. Presently, Andaman and Nicobar Islands administration has 22 vessels comprising of 18
passenger vessels and 4 passenger-cum-cargo vessels, Union Territory of Lakshadweep has 5
vessels comprising 1 passenger-cum-cargo vessel, 3 passenger vessels and one bunker barge. The
Committee observes that water transport is the life-line of these groups of islands for their
interconnection with the mainland and within islands. The Committee notes that this sector has
been neglected for so many years without any fund infusion for modernization of the vessels and
purchase of additional vessels. Due to this, the populations of these islands are suffering to a great
extent. The Committee further notes that in the Demand for Grants for the year 2008-09 no
financial allocation has been made for improving the interconnectivity and water transport in
Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep islands. The Committee, therefore, recommends
to the Government of India to take immediate steps for improving inter-islands connectivity of the
islands of Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep for mitigating the problems of connectivity
between these islands. The Committee also recommends that sufficient Budgetary Allocation may
be provided for augmenting the water transport connectivity in these islands.

ANNUAL PLAN 2007-08
(Recommendations at Paras 11 and 15)
5. The Committee observed that out of the RE (2007-08) Plan allocation of Rs.14066.00 crore,
an amount of Rs.11887.44 was spent (provisional) up to 12th March, 2008 which stands at 84.5%
of RE. The overall expenditure profile of the Department is also not showing any encouraging
trends. Out of Rs.16481.85 crore (RE) for the year 2007-08, a sum of Rs.13338.03 crore was
expended (provisional) till the 12th March, 2008 which stands at 81.0% of the RE. This is very
much in contrast to the quantum of expenditure incurred in the year 2006-07 where it stood at
a good 97.9% of RE allocated for that year.

2
6. The Committee finds that despite its earlier recommendations on the aspect of funds
utilization and the need for constant monitoring of projects, the Department of Road Transport and
Highways has done precious little to improve the situation. This is evident from the reply of the
Department with regard to non-utilization of funds that the allocation for road sector is based on
anticipated implementation of projects every year. The Committee is of the opinion that the road
sector plays a vital role in providing good infrastructure in the country. The Committee feels that
submission of routine replies for underutilization of funds and poor performance in achieving the
physical targets is not going to yield any result. Instead of that, the Department may list out the
bottlenecks and draw a strategy to overcome such bottlenecks. The Committee is of the opinion
that active involvement of project executing agencies such as PWD, NHAI and State Governments
would only help the Department in utilizing its fund to the maximum extent. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that proper co-ordination with all these organizations should be maintained
in order to achieve physical targets satisfactorily.
Reply of the Government
7. There was no change at RE Stage in the budgetary allocation of Rs.14066.00 crore
under Plan Head in respect of Department of Road Transport and Highways (DoRT&H). However,
under Non-Plan, the allocation was increased from Rs.2128.20 crore to Rs.22l5.00 crore at RE
Stage for the year 2007-08. Thus, the total allocation (Plan and Non Plan) at RE stage after
deducting recoveries was Rs.16281.00 crore instead of Rs.16481.85 crore as erroneously stated
earlier. Out of Rs.16281.00 crore (RE) for the year 2007-08, a sum of Rs.16018.13 crore was
expended which stood at 98.39% of the RE. The expenditure during 2006-07 was 97.9%.
Therefore, the expenditure during 2007-08 was better than that of the expenditure incurred in
the year 2006-07. All efforts are being made to maintain this expenditure trend during the current
year also.

ANNUAL PLAN 2008-09
(Recommendations at Paras 26 and 27)
11. The Committee notes that the growth of Motor V ehicles in India is unprecedented. The
process of liberalization and globalization augmented the number of vehicles to beyond the
imagination of our planners of road sector development. The infrastructure available is not at all
commensurate with the growth of vehicles. The Committee also notes that the allocation to the
Department is almost static in real terms. There is an increase of 20% in Annual Plan outlay and
7.6% in budgetary support. The above increase in Annual Plan outlay and budgetary support may
not be adequate even to meet the increase in cost. Thus, it poses a great mismatch between the
availability of the road infrastructure and vehicular population.
12. Inadequate development of road sector will result in congested roads, traffic jams, recurring
accidents and chaos in the road sector. Moreover, the development of road infrastructure is
immensely important to sustain the growth of the economy. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Government should allot funds to the Department of Road Transport and
Highways so as to ensure the development of road infrastructure in proportion to the growth of
vehicles. The Committee further recommends that demands of the Department may be acceded to
at the RE stage.
Reply of the Government
13. All efforts would be made to ensure that substantial amount of funds allocated to the
Department during the year 2008-09 is spent by October, 2008. Thereafter, depending upon the
assessment for requirement of funds, demands for additional allocation would be made at the RE
Stage.

4
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
14. The Committee notes that the Department has left the larger issue of huge growth
in number of vehicles and poor road infrastructure unanswered. It feels that shortage of
funds to the roads sector should not dampen the resolve of the Government to evolve
mechanisms for reducing the mismatch between the availability of the road infrastructure
and vehicular population.
NATIONAL HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
(Recommendation at Para 31)
15. The Committee notes that majority of the work of NHDP Phase-II which was conceived
in the year 2003 has yet to be completed. The Committee would like to know the reasons for the
delay and the agencies/officers responsible for it. The Committee recommends that the Government
may take immediate effective steps to complete the project. The Committee also notes that the
NHDP Phase-IV is yet to be approved by the Government however, no reasons therefor have been
given. It is pity that 20000 km, a major part of local NH, is yet to brought to 2 lane standards
under Phase-IV but the project has not been approved till date by the Government. The Committee
recommends that NHDP Phase-IV may be considered by the Government for approval immediately.
The progress of the projects under other phases may be monitored regularly so as to ensure their
timely implementation.
Reply of the Government
16. NHDP Phase-II comprising of 4 laning of 6,161 kms of North South and East West
Corridors and 486 kms of other highways was approved in December, 2003. Thereafter, works of
preparation of Detailed Project Reports was taken up, which normally takes 12 - 15 months. In
difficult terrain conditions like Jammu and Kashmir and reaches involving wild life, it took even
more time. As on 31.05.2008, 4 laning has been completed for 1,740 kms and works in 4,066 kms
are under implementation and work for 841 kms is yet to be awarded.
17. After April, 2007 no work under Phase-II could be awarded due to new policy of
Government to take up all future projects on BOT (toll) basis in the first instance. The balance
841 kms also included 264 kms in J&K, 31 kms in Assam and 201 kms in West Bengal involving
realignment due to wildlife where BOT (toll) may not be feasible. Committee of Secretaries (CoS)
has already recommended on 01.04.2008 to take up 264 kms in J&K and 31 kms in Assam on
BOT (annuity) basis. Approval of CCEA to this is awaited. Action has been initiated to take up
remaining projects on BOT (toll) basis.
18. The progress of implementation of Phase-II contracts has been seriously affected due to
problems of land acquisition in the S tates of Assam, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and
Tamil Nadu, delay in permission for tree cutting in U.P. due to insistence of State Government to
provide 10 metres strip of land for afforestation as also serious problem of law and order in
Assam. Progress of some projects is also affected due to slow progress by contractors and
unprecedented increase in prices of cement, steel and bitumen in recent months. Despite these
problems, works already awarded under NHDP Phase-II are likely to be substantially completed by
December, 2009 excepting some major bridges over Brahmaputra, Kosi and Chambal and Agra
bypass and Dholpur town portion, which are contractually scheduled for completion in 2010.
Keeping in view the law and order situation in Assam, some projects are likely to spell over to
2010. The delays are mainly systemic and can be attributed to various reasons and no specific
agency or officer can be said to be responsible.

5
19. Upgradation/strengthening of 5000 km of single/intermediate/two lane National Highways to
two lane with paved shoulders under NHDP Phase IV-A on BOT (Toll) and BOT (Annuity) basis
has been approved by the Cabinet on 17th July, 2008 — to be taken up on the ratio of 4:1.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
20. The Committee is distressed to note that the much publicized NHDP Phase II started
in the year 2003 is still lingering on for one reason or the other. Completion of just 1740
kms out of the approved 6161 kms after five years under the phase II present a pathetic
picture of this project. The Committee feels that such a slow progress is not going to
yield the desired result in the road sector. Due to poor and bad shape, our national
highways are not in a position to bear the rising number of vehicles. The Committee also
hopes that at least the ongoing road projects of NHAI such as the grade separator at
Badarpur Border related to Commonwealth Games 2010 in the capital region will be
completed in time.

25. The Committee notes the reply of the Department. Though the Department has

(Recommendation at Para 41)
26. The Committee is unhappy with the delay in finalizing the Detailed Project Report on
Mughal Road in Jammu and Kashmir as a result of which, the competent authority could not
sanction the project. The Government, however, has not given any reason as to why there was
delay in finalizing the Detailed Project Report. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Department to apprise the Committee about those reasons and action taken in the matter. The
Committee desires that the Department should fine tune its systems and procedures to avoid such
delays.
Reply of the Government
27. The 84 km long Mughal Road is to connect Shopian in Pulwama District of Kashmir Valley
with the remote areas of Poonch and Rajouri Districts of Jammu. The preliminary cost indicated
as approved in PM package was Rs.159.00 crore on the basis of feasibility report of 2001 and
reconnaissance survey conducted by M/s  RITES. The detailed survey and investigations of 84 km
road was required for preparation of Detailed Project Report. The stretch is in the remote areas
and terrain is hilly and difficult. The working period is very limited in the State of J&K due to
weather conditions. Further, this stretch is very near to the Pakistan border. Therefore, extra care

7
was required during survey due to security reasons. Therefore, submission of DPR has taken time
although Ministry has requested State PWD in July, 2006, September, 2007, November, 2007,
February, 2008 and March, 2008 for submission of Detailed Project Report. The DPR has now
been submitted by Government of J&K for an amount of Rs.638.85 crore in March, 2008. The
work is proposed to be considered under Economic Importance scheme. The Centre and State
shares are fifty percent each. The EFC procedure will be followed and CCEA clearance be obtained
for sanctioning of the project. The State Government has already awarded the work, which is
targeted to be completed by April, 2010.

NATIONAL HIGHWAYS (ORIGINAL) WORKS — NH(O)
(Recommendation at Para 45)
29. The Committee is not happy with the mere 15.90% increase in allocation for the
maintenance of National Highways. The Committee was informed that an amount of Rs. 2280.00 crore
is required for maintenance and repair of roads annually, The Committee is of the opinion that
Government should give adequate importance for the maintenance and repair of non-NHDP
highways to ensure that investment made in the NHs does not go waste. The Committee
recommends that one-third of the cess collected for the financing NHDP projects should be
allocated for the maintenance and repair of highways. The Committee desires that the Department
should take up the issue with the Planning Commission for getting one third portion of the cess
collected for the maintenance and repair of National Highways as this non-NHDP National
Highways are considered as lifeline of Indian transport sector.
Reply of the Government
30. The matter regarding apportionment of one-third of the cess collected on fuel towards the
maintenance and repair of National Highways (non-NHDP highways) was taken up with Planning
Commission. Keeping in view that this may result in some investment gap in the NHDP funding,
the Planning Commission was requested to agree in-principle for allocating extra funds to meet this
gap. In a meeting held on 22nd April, 2008, a Committee headed by Shri Anwarul Hoda, Member,
Planning Commission has been constituted, to prepare a revised financing plan for the National
Highways Development Project (NHDP) involving the cess fund, duly keeping in view the fund
requirement for maintenance and repair of NHs.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
31. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and urges the Planning
Commission to take a view in this regard at the earliest.

(Recommendations at Para 54)

bills for the purchase of petroleum products. In this way, the Committee apprehends that the

37. The Committee is at loss to see that the issue of under reporting of cess collected

Recommendation at Para 55
38. The Committee further notes that Railways is a profit-making Public Sector Enterprise. The
Committee could not, therefore, understand the rationale behind the pooling of a major chunk of
the Central Road Fund with the Railways. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Railways which itself capable to undertake developmental works, wherever required, may do so
from its own resources/profits instead of seeking allocation from the Central Road Fund.
Reply of the Government
39. Allocation of resources from the Central Road Fund for different purposes is governed by

9
the Section 10 of the Central Road Fund Act, 2000. According to Section 10 (1) (viii), the Central
Government is responsible for allocation of:
(a) fifty per cent of the cess on high speed diesel oil for the development of rural roads
in such manner as may be prescribed; and
(b) the balance amount of fifty per cent of cess on high speed diesel oil and the entire
cess collected on petrol as follows:
(i) an amount equal to fifty seven and one-half per cent of such sum for the
development and maintenance of National Highways;
(ii) an amount equal to twelve and one-half per cent for the construction of road
either under or over the railways by means of a bridge and erection of safety
works at unmanned, rail-road crossings; and
(iii) the balance thirty per cent on development and maintenance of roads other than
National Highways and out of this amount, ten per cent, i.e. three per cent of
the total share of State roads shall be kept as reserve by the Central Government
for allocation to States for implementation of State road schemes of Inter-State
and Economic Importance to be approved by the Central Government in terms
of clauses (iii) and (iv) of this section.
40. It may be observed from the above that the Railways are entitled to a specific amount from
the Central Road Fund for the construction of road either under or over Railways by means of
a bridge and erection of safety works at unmanned rail-road crossing. Since this is an allocation
governed by the statutory provision, the Railways cannot be denied of their share of the allocation
from the Central Road Fund.

ROAD SAFETY
(Recommendation at Para 64)
42. The Committee feels that school children are the best messiahs for preaching road
safety to their parents. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the road safety campaign
may give adequate importance to this aspect and the Department may rope in schools and
school children to spread awareness for road safety. The work done by the NGOs for raising
road safety awareness may also be given due publicity in media and local newspapers. This
may ensure the better functioning of NGOs and the public in general will keep watch on their
activities.
Reply of the Government
43. To inculcate the road safety habits amongst the school children, a scheme for setting up
Road Safety Clubs in school has been formulated and action for approval of the scheme by the
Planning Commission has been initiated. Apart from this, the quiz competition, essay competition,
drawing and painting competition are being sanctioned as activities for promoting road safety
awareness by NGOs on regular basis. The NGOs are to abide by the terms and conditions annexed

10
with the sanction letter as per which they have to give due publicity in the Press and other possible
media before starting the sanction activities. At the time of sanctioning grant to the NGOs for road
safety programme, a request is being made to the Transport Department of the concerned State
for strict monitoring of functioning of the NGOs.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
44. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hope that the Planning
Commission will give timely approval to the scheme of setting up Road Safety Clubs.
REFRESHER TRAINING OF DRIVERS IN UNORGANISED SECTOR AND HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
(Recommendation at Para 67)
45. The Committee feels that this is a welcome step. The Committee recommends that the
number of organizations sponsored by the Ministry is very low and insufficient compared to the
vastness of our transport sector. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government may
endeavour to finance at least one NGO in each of the districts of the country for imparting
refresher course to the drivers of Heavy Motor V ehicles. The Committee also recommends that a
proper monitoring mechanism may be put in place to ensure that the organizations are actually
imparting training to the drivers.
Reply of the Government
46. The number of drivers sanctioned under this scheme for imparting training is constantly
increasing. For the year 2008-09, the target fixed is 75000 drivers against 57850 drivers sanctioned
during 2007-08. However, due to fund constraint, it is not feasible to sanction grant to one NGO
in each district of the country. For proper monitoring of the implementation of the scheme, at the
time of sanction of grant to the NGO for imparting refresher training to the driver, Transport
Department of the concerned State Government is requested for proper monitoring. The second
and final installment is released to the NGO only after getting the Final Action Taken Report from
the concerned State.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
47. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and recommends that more funds
should be allocated for imparting training to drivers. Further, monitoring of NGOs by way
of obtaining utilisation certificates may be enforced.
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
(Recommendation at Para 70)
48. The Committee notes that the Planning Commission has discontinued the scheme of
Model Driving Training Schools. The Committee may be apprised of the reasons for the
discontinuance of the scheme. The Committee would also like to know whether any alternative
schemes are proposed by the Planning Commission to fill the gap of Model Driving Training
Schools.
Reply of the Government
49. Being a Centrally sponsored scheme, the Planning Commission has dropped the scheme of

11
Model Driver Training School. The revised scheme with certain changes for setting up Model
Driver Training School is being formulated and will be sent to the Planning Commission for their
approval shortly.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
50. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that the revised scheme of
Model Driver Training School will be formulated on priority and the Committee may be appraised
about the new scheme once it is approved.
(Recommendation at Para 71)
51. The States where Model Driving Training Schools were sanctioned may be asked to
complete the projects in a time bound manner and funds may be allotted accordingly.
Reply of the Government
52. Out of 13, two schools have become operational. The financial assistance sanctioned to
schools in Assam, Karnataka, West Bengal, Himachal Pradesh, Uttaranchal, Uttar Pradesh, Orissa
and Nagaland has been released to them substantially and these schools are likely to be operational
very soon. A request to facilitate the progress of the sanctioned project for setting up of school
in Madhya Pradesh and Haryana are made on regular basis.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
53. The Committee recommends that all the 13 schools should be operational at the
earliest and other States may be persuaded to set up the schools.
NATIONAL HIGHWAYS ACCIDENT RELIEF SERVICE SCHEME
(Recommendation at Para 75)
54. The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department for providing trauma care.
At the very same time, the Committee feels that the present allocation of fund of Rs.2.20 crore
for the trauma care is too inadequate. The Government should try to augment the funding for
trauma care. The Committee is constrained to note the tardy progress made in purchasing cranes
and ambulances. The Committee also recommends that the formalities for purchasing cranes and
ambulances may be completed at the earliest so that the trauma care facilities can be put in place
without further delay.
Reply of the Government
55. The specifications for small size crane, 10-ton crane and ambulances have been reviewed
and order for procurement of 100 ambulances, 30 Nos. of 10-ton cranes and 19 small size
cranes have been placed during 2007-08 for the year 2008-09. The tender process for procurement
of 10-ton crane, small size crane and ambulances (to be provided by this Department to the
identified hospitals by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare) under this scheme has been
initiated.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
56. The Committee notes the reply of the Department.

12
NATIONAL DATA BASE NETWORK
(Recommendation at Para 78)
57. Application of information technology for the development of the country is the mantra of
the day. Of course, the Department has taken initiatives in the right direction way back in the year
2001. The Committee notes that till now, only a few States have embarked on the course of
implementing IT enabled systems for driving licences and registration certificates. We have the
resources, talent and expertise in the IT field. The Committee wonders what prevent the
Government from implementing the IT-enabled systems in the Road Transport Sector. The
Committee notes that target for completion of the IT-enabled systems is 2009 which is not far
away. The Committee has doubt whether the Government will be able to meet the target which
they could not do for the last seven years. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the matters
may be reviewed at the highest level and steps may be taken to remove the bottlenecks. The
Committee also recommends that those States which are not implementing the IT-enabled Driving
Licence (DL) and Registration Certificate (RC) may be persuaded highlighting the benefit and
importance of IT-enabled system for DL and RC. The Committee also recommends that some
incentive scheme may be developed in such a way that those States which are implementing the
IT enabled systems should get sanction for more projects and schemes.
Reply of the Government
58. For strengthening of National Database Network relating to Transport Sector, the matter is
being reviewed at the level of Secretary (RT&H) and Joint Secretary (Transport). For issue of
Smart Card based Driving License and Registration Certificate and to have their inter-operability
through out the country, meetings are being arranged with all the States/UTs to emphasize the need
for its early implementation and to discuss and eradicate the problems being faced by them.
Recently, an amount of Rs 299.50 lakh was released to NIC for the work of Data Migration to
National Standards in the Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) in the country to ensure that entire
data conforms to the National Standard. The project will be located at Delhi and data from 35
States/UTs will be brought on electronic media. This project will be completed within a period of
nine months. On 31-3-2008 the EFC meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Secretary
(RT&H) and the EFC proposal for creation of State Registers and National Register at a cost of
Rs.148.00 crore was approved.

59. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that the project will be
completed in time.

(Recommendation at Para 81)
60. The Committee hopes that the steps taken by the Ministry will bear fruits in the near future.
The allocation of Rs.5.80 crore for the year 2008-09 is very meager compared to the vehicular
population of the country. The Committee recommends that more allocation need to be given to
the objectives of schemes so that the road safety and pollution control is achieved in its optimum

Reply of the Government
61. Under this scheme, road safety equipments such as interceptors and pollution testing

13
equipments such as smoke meters and gas analysers are provided to the States/UTs for
enforcement of road safety laws and Pollution Under Control norms. The recommendation of the
Committee for enhanced allocation has been noted. It will be taken into consideration while
finalizing the BE for 2009-2010.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
62. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that the Department
will give due importance to road safety equipments and pollution control instruments while
finalizing its BE for the year 2009-10.
NEW SCHEMES OF ELEVENTH PLAN
(Recommendation at Para 85)
63. The Committee welcomes the intention of the Government to set up more inspection and
maintenance centres to identify the vehicles which do not meet the emission and safety norms
subject to the condition that these new centres should not override the authority of State RTOs.
The Committee feels that some monitoring or regulatory authority should be put in place before
these centres become operational as there is a possibility that these centres can harass the vehicle
owners in connivance with the vehicle manufacturers to change their vehicles by citing one or
other reasons. The Committee also recommends that a proper mechanism should also be set up
to monitor the allocation is spent meaningfully.
Reply of the Government
64. The suggestion given by the Committee shall be kept in view while finalizing the proposal
for setting up of I & M Centres.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
65. The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
NEW SCHEMES OF ELEVENTH PLAN
(Recommendation at Para 89)
66. The Committee is very much disappointed about the negligence on the part of the
Government in promoting public transport system in the country. The Committee is of the opinion
that cities are jammed with rising number of private vehicles and the villages are not even getting
adequate public transport facility. The Committee once again reiterates its earlier recommendation
that in the absence of user-friendly public transports, the people in the country are resorting to
excessive use of private vehicles and this has put the roads under undue pressure. The Committee
observes that most of the investment on roads is being extracted from the public itself but the
returns accruing to the users are not equitable. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
efforts of the Government should focus on developing public transport, which discourages
excessive use of private vehicles. The Government should adopt a methodology, whereby, in the
more densely populated States, the rich and the affluent are asked to pay more for keeping more
than one vehicle.
Reply of the Government
67. Road Transport is a State subject. However, keeping in view the need for strengthening

14
public transport system in the country, an amount of Rs.24.99 crore has been kept for the year
2008-09 for providing financial assistance to the S tates/UTs to strengthen their public transport
system subject to the condition that the States are committed to take certain reform measures
required for the sector. A broad scheme in this regard is being formulated by this Department.
Earlier, the views of the Committee regarding differential taxes for the owners having more than
one vehicle have been brought to the notice of the States/UTs for necessary action at their end.
While finalizing the broad scheme for providing the financial assistance to the State,
recommendation of the Committee would be taken into account so that the States would have to
take such reform measures to avail financial assistance from Central Government.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
68. The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
CREATION OF NATIONAL ROAD SAFETY BOARD
(Recommendation at Para 92)
69. The Committee feels that the time has come for the creation of the much talked about
National Road Safety Board as the number of road accidents on national highways is increasing
in an alarming manner. The Committee recommends that the Department should pursue the matter
vigorously and take necessary actions to establish this Board at the earliest.
Reply of the Government
70. A Committee under the chairmanship of Shri S. Sundar, former Secretary, MOST was set
up in the year 2005 to deliberate and to make recommendations for creation of a dedicated body
on Road Safety and Traffic Management. The Committee submitted its report on 20-2-2007 inter-
alia recommending the creation of a National Road Safety and Traffic Management Board through
an Act of Parliament to oversee the road safety activities in the country. The Committee of
Secretaries (CoS) in its meeting held on 4-3-2008 has considered the proposal of this Department
for creation of the Board and has in-principle, accepted the same. As directed by the CoS, a note
for creation of the Board is being finalized for consideration of the Expenditure Finance Committee
(EFC). The EFC would look into the details of the Board including the mechanism of flow of funds
to the States/UTs from National Road Safety Fund.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
71. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and opines that the National Road
Safety and Traffic Management Board is the need of the hour and Department of Road
Transport is requested to pursue the case with the EFC and see that the formalities
regarding having such a Board are completed quickly.
TOLL TAX ON BRIDGES AND NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
(Recommendation at Para 94)
72. The Committee once again recommends that once the capital and interest is recovered, the
users’ fee must be discontinued. The Committee is of the opinion that there is a need for
establishment of a regulator to determine the reasonable return to the investor on road projects
which is being considered as a yardstick for fixation of toll. The Committee appreciates that in
view of the resource crunch being faced by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and

15
there is a genuine need for generation of additional revenue by the Ministry. Whenever any National
Highway is constructed, it leads to huge value addition to the land adjoining the National Highway
and these benefits of addition in value have so far been enjoyed by private agencies only. The
Government should also get advantage of the appreciation of land value because it is the taxpayer’s
money that has led to the value addition of that property. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Government may explore the possibility of imposing some cess/tax on land adjoining
National Highways which is being utilized for commercial purpose on annual basis. This could
serve as a permanent source of income for the Government and the revenue so generated could
be ploughed back for the construction and maintenance of National Highways in the country.
Provision of ducting at the time of construction of National Highways for laying telephone and
electric cables also leads to value addition and can be explored for generating more funds for the
road sector. These measures may go a long way to meet the resource gap for maintenance and
construction of National Highways in the country.
Reply of the Government
73. The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee had made the same
recommendation while considering the Demands for Grants for the year 2004-05 of the Ministry
of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways. The recommendation was as follows:
“The Committee recommends that the Government may explore the possibility of imposing
some cess/tax on land adjoining National Highways, which is being utilized for commercial
purpose on annual basis. This could serve as a permanence source of income for the
Government and the revenue so generated could be ploughed back only for the construction
of National Highways in the country.”
74. The levy of cess/tax in respect of the indirect benefit like appreciation in land value due
to the coming of National infrastructure like National Highways in a nearby area is a complex issue
having legal and socio-economic implications. Considering the complexity of the issue, the above
recommendation was referred to the Ministry of Law and their advice was as follows:
(i) The land adjoining to National Highways in most cases will be agricultural or fallow
land. The power to levy taxes on such land and building is covered by the State list
and State Governments are only concerned.
(ii) The power to acquire land under the NH Act, 1956 is restricted and limited for
development, maintenance, management or operation of the National Highways.
Acquisition of land for the purpose of other activities is outside the scope of NH
Act, 1956. The land acquisition is to be done as per LA Act, 1894 if the intention is
to acquire land for construction of hotels and restaurants, etc. by the side of National
Highways.
(iii) The capital gain at the time of sale of adjoining land is taken as income for the
purposes of the Income Tax Act excluding agricultural income. Tax on capital gain is
already covered under the Income Tax Act.
75. In view of the above, it was decided not to take any further action on the recommendation
of the Committee.
76. As regards the recommendation of the Committee regarding discontinuation of the levy of
user fee, it is informed that the National Highways Act, 1956 provides for the levy of the user fee
(toll) for services or benefits referred in relation to the use of National Highway sections, bridges,
tunnels etc. The provision for discontinuation of levy of user fee was available in the National
Highways (Fees for the use of Permanent Bridges) Rules, 1992. These Rules were superseded at

16
the time of notification of the National Highways (Fees for the use of National Highway sections
and permanent bridges — Public Funded Project) Rules, 1997. According to Rule 11  of these
Rules, fee shall be collected in perpetuity by the executing agency. At present, there is no provision
for discontinuation of the fee in any of the user fee (toll) related Rules.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
77. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and desires to know the yardstick
with the Department for fixing the user fees on national highways. The Department is also
silent on the issue of creation of a revolving fund for financing of major road projects. The
Committee expects the Department to come out with some practical solutions to do away

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport,
Tourism and Culture, having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Forty-fifth Report on “Action Taken by the Government on the
Recommendations/Observations of the Committee contained in its One Hundred and Thirty-sixth
Report on Demands for Grants 2008-09 of the Ministry of Tourism”.
2. The One Hundred and Thirty-sixth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented to the Parliament on the
28th April, 2008.
3. The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained on its
One Hundred and Thirty-sixth Report were received from the Ministry of Tourism on the
27th August, 2008.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the
18th December, 2008.

REPORT
This Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
observations/recommendations as contained in its One Hundred Thirty-sixth Report on Demands for
Grants (2008-09) (Demand No.93) of the Ministry of Tourism, which was presented to the
Parliament on 28th April, 2008.
2. Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on 27th August, 2008 in
respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report. These have been
categorized as follows:—
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 9, 23, 24, 51, 52, 54, 61, 68, 69, 75 and 76 Total-11
(ii) Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in
view of the Government replies:
Para No. 101 T otal-1
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have
not been accepted by the Committee:
Para Nos. 14 and 22 T otal-2
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are
still awaited:
Para Nos. 30, 37, 38, 58, 64, 82, 83, 86, 92 and 97 Total-10
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which
have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the
earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each
item of the action taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry of Tourism. The recommendations
of the Committee contained in its One Hundred Thirty Sixth Report, action taken thereon by the
Government and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of action taken
have been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS AND ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2008-09
(Recommendation at Para 9)
5. The Committee observes that the Ministry of Tourism projected a requirement of
Rs.5405.58 crore (10% basis) and Rs.6569.61 crore (20% basis) for the entire Eleventh Plan
against this requirement, the Planning Commission approved an allocation of Rs.5156.00 crore for
carrying out major activities of the Ministry viz.  Augmentation of Tourist infrastructure,

allocated. The Committee deplores the tendency of Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance
for imposing cuts on the amounts demanded by the Ministry. This mismatch between projected
amount and sanctioned outlay may result in widening further the gap between the tourism potential

2
and development of tourism synergies for achieving the goals. The Committee feels that in order
to attain the National growth targets in the Eleventh Plan period, huge planned funding is required.
Thus, the Government spending for the Ministry of Tourism will have to be significantly stepped-
up from the present level to meet the investment targets. The Committee, therefore, strongly
recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should be provided with Rs.6569.61 crore (20% basis)
by the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance for the Eleventh Plan Period as per their
original demand. The Committees also recommends the Ministry of Tourism to take appropriate
caution and remedial action to absorb in time the allocation made to them.

6. The Ministry accepts the recommendation that Government spending on tourism needs to
be stepped up with increased plan outlay.
7. The views of the Hon’ble Committee has been conveyed to the Ministry of Finance and
Planning Commission for providing Rs.6569.61 crore (20% basis) as per original proposal for the

8. The Ministry is taking conscious efforts to incur evenly paced utilization, which was
evident in 2007-08 with Ministry achieving upto 42% in second quarter, 69% in third quarter and

Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
9. The Committee notes that as per the recommendation of the Committee the Ministry
of Tourism has requested the Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission for providing
Rs.6569.61 crore (20% basis) as per original proposal for the Eleventh Five Year Plan. The

Planning Commission for allocating the projected outlay. The Committee hopes that with
the allocation of the projected outlay for the Plan, the Ministry will be able to fully exploit
the tourism potentials besides developing tourist infrastructure in the country.
(Recommendation at Para 14)
10. The Committee notes that during 2007-08, the plan outlay of Rs.996.62 crore of Ministry
of Tourism was not subjected to any cut at RE stage. However, the Committee notes that during
the year 2007-08, out of the budgeted allocation of Rs.996.62 crore, the Ministry could spent
Rs.658.55 crore upto December, 2007 which clearly indicates the poor fiscal management in the
Ministry of Tourism. The Committee observes that the major portion of the budgetary outlays has
been utilized during the last quarter of the financial year. The Committee disapproves the tendency
of spending funds desperately towards the end of the financial year especially, in the months of
February and March. The Committee expects that the maximum amount of plan outlay would be
utilized suitably and substantially during the first two quarters of the financial year so that the
Ministry will be in a position to demand for higher allocations of the funds at RE stage for

Promotion and publicity of tourism in the country. The Committee therefore, recommends the
Ministry to plan and incur their expenditure uniformly so that funds are utilized appropriately
throughout the year and the Ministry should shun the practice of incurring expenditure
indiscriminately towards the last quarter of the financial year. This way no alibi will be provided
to the Ministry of Finance to reduce the allocation at RE Stage. The Committee also recommends
that the Ministry should do away with procedural hurdles and maintain close liaison for the purpose
of review, monitoring, implementation and coordinating of projects/schemes to achieve the
envisaged targets.

3

AUGMENTATION OF TOURISM INFRASTRUCTURE
(Recommendation at Para 22)

not in a position to spend the entire amount in such a short period and therefore have unspent
balance lying with them. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the release of the funds to
the States should be made on time so that they could utilize the amount rationally under proper

with the State Government, so as to obtain utilization certificates and to safeguard that money

4

18. The Committee feels that waiting unduly long for utilization certificates would

19. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is making efforts to develop quality
tourism infrastructure at major tourist destinations and circuits for developing tourist products and
providing better services to both domestic and international tourists. The Committee observes that

and can ensure consequential development of the infrastructure of the destinations and circuits. The
Committee feels that the infrastructure development holds the key to India’s sustain growth in the
tourism sector, therefore, tourist sites and destinations needs to be carefully selected on the basis
of their potential to provide all infrastructural facilities required by the tourists within such

inherent potential in tourism, then it must provide exclusive quality tourism product and destinations
comparable with other Asian countries like Singapore, Malaysia, Maldives, Thailand and China. As

dissemination is required in addition to hospitality and the scope and reach of the domestic tourism

Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to develop quality tourism at identified tourist
circuits and destinations with focus on mega destinations and circuits that match international
standards and satisfy the domestic and international tourists. The aggressive marketing and publicity
of these destinations and circuits should also be done to generate a niche market of Indian tourism
products. The Committee also urges the Ministry that while selecting a destination or a circuit they
should attach priority for harmonious growth and development of all the Regions and States.

21. Developed destinations/circuits are also being promoted in domestic and overseas markets.

and circuits and projects with Jawahar Lal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) for

24. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is making efforts with the State

RELAXATION OF THE RESTRICTED AREA PERMIT (RAP)/PROTECTED AREA PERMIT
(PAP)/INNER LINE PERMIT (ILP) REGIME
(Recommendation at Para 64)
50. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is in constant touch with Ministry of
Home Affairs to relax/abolish the requirement of permit system in the country as the growth of
international tourism is based on development of tourism in that destination. The Committee is of
the view that foreign tourists constitute an important component of tourists who wish to visit the
country specially the North Eastern States and Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands.
The restrictions on foreigners to stay beyond permitted period and visiting only selected islands/
regions/destination has discouraged the foreign tourists arrival in the country. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that in order to optimally exploit the potential of tourism in these islands/
regions/destinations, the restrictions on the foreigners on visiting the islands/regions may be
removed and they may be permitted to stay/ enjoy the beauty of the islands/regions/destination for
a longer periods. The Committee also feels that opening up new islands/regions/destination for
foreigners also needs to be given priority. The Committee recommends the Ministry of Tourism to
vigorously pursue the matter of review of liberalization of the entire RAP/P AP/ILP regime at the
highest level in the Ministry of Home Affairs which act as a hindrance to the growth and
development of domestic and international tourism to those regions. The Committee may be
apprised of the outcome in the matter from time to time.
Reply of the Government
51. In order to boost tourism in these areas, the issues for which relaxation/abolition of the
RAP/PAP regime, is being sought, are:
• Tourists desirous of visiting areas having the RAP/PAP regime are required to travel in
a group of minimum of 4. Some of the places also require that they should be
accompanied by a liaison officer. In fact several areas such as Nanda Devi in
Uttarakhand and some areas of Sikkim do not permit individual tourists. The requirement
should be removed as the trend today is increasingly towards individual tourists.
• The maximum number of days that the tourist is permitted to stay at these places is
also restricted to 7, 10 or 15 days (only exception are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
where they are permitted 45 days). This restriction should be removed so that tourists
can visit these areas at leisure.
• The routes for regions covered by RAP/PAP regime are also delineated by the Ministry
of Home Affairs due to which the tourists are restricted from visiting other interesting
places which may fall off these routes. This restriction should also be removed.
• Some of these States mentioned above even have an Inner Line Permit which has to
be taken by the domestic tourists visiting these areas. There is an urgent need to
completely relax/withdraw this permit as growth of international tourism to a region is
based on development of tourism in that destination.
52. The entire area of Arunachal Pradesh is covered by the Protected Area Regime under the
Foreigners (Protected Areas) Order, 1958. No foreigners can enter or stay in the State without
obtaining a permit from the competent authority.
53. In this regard, the Government of India, in consultation with all concerned has now decided
to open the following tour circuits for the foreign tourists in Arunachal Pradesh.
1. Along — Mechukha.

12
2. Existing Pasighat — Jenging — Yiungkiong to be extended upto Tuting.
3. Daporijo — Nacho Circuit via Taliha and Sayum.
4. Ziro — Palin — Nyapin — Sangram — Kaloriang.
5. Doimukh — Sagalee — Pakke Kasang — Seppa.
It has also been decided to delegate powers to the Government of Arunachal Pradesh for
issue of Protected Area Permit (PAP) in respect of the following:—
(a) To the visiting foreign tourists in a group of two or more persons (as against the
existing requirement of group strength of four or more persons) for a maximum period
of 30 days.
(b) To a group of two foreign tourists even if they are not married couples and to
foreigners married to Indian nationals belonging to the State of Arunachal Pradesh for
visiting the State on tourist visas.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
54. The Committee notes that although the Government has relaxed the permit system
in the Arunachal Pradesh to the visiting foreign tourists but for the rest of the North-
eastern region and Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands, it has not undertaken
a review exercise as suggested by the Committee. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Government should consider relaxation/withdrawal of permit system as growth of
International tourism in a region is based on the easy accessibility of that area to the
tourist.

condition and suggest measures to improve connectivity to all major destinations/heritage sites with
the National Highways. The Ministry of Tourism has provided a list of 11 roads to the group for
improvement and upgradation which connects the tourist destinations and circuits including heritage
sites. The Committee is aware that improvement and upgradation of State roads, is the
responsibility of State Government. Therefore, the Ministry of Tourism should impress upon the
respective State Governments/UTs to improve the condition of such roads and Government of
India should consider the proposals for improvement of State roads under Central Road fund
Scheme.

should be well connected with the rail, road and air to ensure the easy accessibility to these places.

stations connecting these mega destinations The Ministry of Civil Aviation should develop
infrastructure facilities at airports to meet the rising air traffic requirements and quality of service at

MULTICIPLICTY OF TAXES
(Recommendation at Para 86)
78. The Committee is constrained to notes that luxury tax on hotel, V A T on food and beverages
and on Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) and higher rate of taxes on tourists transport vehicles in the
States have adverse effect on the growth of tourism. The Committee, however, is perturbed to note
that even after repeated recommendations of the Committee, the Government has not been able to
do much to rationalize the tax regime, which is ailing the tourism sector at large. The Ministry of
Tourism has forwarded two proposals for consideration of Empowered Committee of State Finance
Ministers and Department of Road Transport and Highways respectively, in this regard and a
decision is awaited. The Committee strongly criticizes the lackadaisical approach of the Government
in the matter which has adversely affected the growth of tourism and hospitality sector in the
country. The Committee reiterates that the Government must provide a level playing field to the
tourism and hospitality sector including tourist transport by attempting to rationalize taxes or
eliminate the disparity in tax treatment as levied by the different States and Union Territories. The
Committee recommends the Ministry to pursue vigorously the matter of rationalization of taxes with
the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers till the matter is favourably resolved. The
Committee also recommends the Government to set up an Empowered Group for rationalization of
roads and transport taxes on tourist vehicles.

and security is paramount and needs to be looked into seriously. The Committee is aware about the
linkages between Centre and States in the federal set-up and appreciates the efforts of the Ministry
in persuading the States for creation of tourist police force for ensuring the safety and security of
the tourists. The Committee also notes that the Ministry of Tourism is formulating guidelines
regarding formation of tourist police force and has taken several steps to curb the menace of

the safety and security related issues in a big way. The Committee also desires that the police
personnel of the States should also be provided special tourist oriented training.
